description: Discord-like community system + messaging: community model, channels, membership tiers, moderation, DMs, group chats, real-time infrastructure, roles/permissions, and gap analysis against current schema
sources: phase14_6b_creatoros_data_ontology.json (column-level schema for communities, channels, channel_messages, conversations, conversation_participants, direct_messages)
CreatorOS_1NIZXMZR.json (Google Doc Tab 3: PRD community specs, Tab 8: platform kernel vision)
shared/schema.ts (GitHub main branch — Drizzle ORM source of truth)

community_model.description: Discord-like branded community spaces owned by creators. Each community belongs to a creator (or business entity), contains channels organized by category, and supports free and paid membership tiers with channel-level access gating.

critical_gaps: No owner_user_id FK — communities are ownerless in schema
No business_id FK — no connection to business entity
No membership table — anyone can access any community

core.name: id
core.note: Align with other new tables using UUID PKs

core.name: business_id
core.note: Optional business entity ownership. Null for personal communities.

core.name: welcome_message
core.note: Message shown to new members on join

core.name: rules
core.note: Community rules displayed during onboarding and in sidebar

core.name: invite_code
core.note: Shareable invite code for invite_only communities

membership_tiers.label: Free
membership_tiers.description: Open access to the community. May be gated to invite_only communities but no payment required.

membership_tiers.label: Paid Membership
membership_tiers.description: Recurring subscription unlocking premium channels and content. Price set by creator per community.
membership_tiers.price_range_note: Creator sets price. Typical range $5-$99/month based on niche.
membership_tiers.note: Aligns with product type 'community' in product_types_commerce_canon.json. Community is one of the 10 product types in CreatorOS.

channel_types.label: Text Channel
channel_types.description: Standard Discord-like text chat channel with messages, reactions, pins, and threading.
channel_types.implementation_note: channels and channel_messages tables exist. Basic messaging works. No reactions, no threading, no media attachments.

channel_types.label: Voice Channel
channel_types.description: Real-time voice communication channel. Drop-in model (join/leave, not scheduled calls).

channel_types.label: Video Channel
channel_types.description: Real-time video communication channel. Screen sharing, camera toggle, gallery view.

channel_types.label: Announcement Channel
channel_types.description: Read-only for regular members. Only creator/admins can post. Members can react. Used for updates, releases, events.

channel_types.label: Forum Channel
channel_types.description: Thread-based discussion channel. Each post creates a thread. Upvotes, tags, solved markers. For Q&A, feedback, feature requests.

channel_types.label: Stage Channel
channel_types.description: Broadcast-style channel for AMAs, panels, webinars. One or few speakers, many listeners. Raise-hand model for audience participation.
channel_types.infrastructure_needed: WebRTC with selective forwarding unit (SFU) for scale

permissions.description: Layered permission model: community-level defaults, channel-level overrides, role-based grants.

layers.description: Default permissions for all members in this community. Set by community owner.
Per-channel permission overrides. Specific roles or membership tiers can be granted or denied per channel.
Named roles with bundled permissions. Assigned to members by community owner or admins.
layers.custom_role_note: Creator can define named roles with arbitrary permission bundles. Roles are ordered by hierarchy level (higher overrides lower).

channel_model.description: Channels live inside communities. Each channel has a type, belongs to an optional category, and contains messages. Channel-level permissions override community defaults.

critical_gaps: No position/sort_order field for ordering in sidebar
No category_id FK for channel grouping

core.name: last_message_at

Rich link preview or embedded content (YouTube, tweet, etc.).
System-generated messages (user joined, channel created, settings changed).
Inline poll within a channel message.

No threading/reply_to support (DMs have reply_to_message_id, channel messages do not)
No edit tracking (DMs have is_edited, channel messages do not)
No attachments array or media_url fields

typing_indicators.note: Client sends typing.start, server broadcasts to channel. Auto-expires after debounce_ms if no new keystrokes.

history.description: Message history access, pagination, and search.

pagination.note: Load newest messages first, scroll up to load older. Cursor-based for consistency under concurrent writes.

search.note: Full-text search on message content. Postgres tsvector or external search (Meilisearch/Typesense) for scale.

pinned_messages.current_note: channel_messages.is_pinned boolean exists. No API for listing pinned messages, no pin limit, no pin attribution (who pinned it).

membership.description: Community membership model: who belongs, at what tier, with what permissions. Bridges the community product type to the entitlement system.

columns.name: name
columns.note: e.g., 'Silver', 'Gold', 'VIP'

columns.note: Null = no annual option

gating_model.description: How membership tier controls access to channels and content.
rules: Free members see and access all channels marked minimum_tier = null or minimum_tier = 'free'
Paid members see and access all channels their tier level unlocks
Channel minimum_tier references a community_tiers.name or the special value 'free'
Private channels (is_private = true) require explicit role-based access regardless of tier
Announcement channels are read-only for non-admin roles regardless of tier
A user's effective permissions = community_defaults UNION role_grants MINUS channel_denials
gating_model.access_check_pseudocode: can_access(user, channel) => is_member(user, channel.community) AND (channel.minimum_tier is null OR user_tier >= channel.minimum_tier) AND (NOT channel.is_private OR has_explicit_access(user, channel)) AND NOT is_banned(user, channel.community)

pricing_integration.description: How community membership pricing connects to the commerce system.
flow: Creator creates community tier with monthly/annual price
System creates Stripe Product + Price objects
Stripe Checkout session created, consumer completes payment
Webhook confirms payment, system creates community_members record with tier = paid
On cancellation: entitlement marked for expiry at period end
On period end without renewal: tier downgraded to free, premium channel access revoked
pricing_integration.note: No Stripe integration exists in CreatorOS. No payment processing at all. This entire flow is aspirational.

moderation.description: Content moderation for community channels and DMs. Not implemented. Module 15 in product architecture.

auto_mod.description: Automated moderation rules applied to channel messages before they become visible.

rules.description: Detect and auto-remove spam messages (repeated content, excessive mentions, link spam).
Block or flag messages containing words from a custom blocklist.
rules.note: Creator defines per-community blocklist. Default empty.

rules.description: Control which links can be posted. Allowlist or blocklist mode.
Prevent message flooding. Configurable via channel slowmode_seconds.
Flag or block messages that are predominantly uppercase (shouting).

manual_mod.description: Moderator and admin actions on messages and members.

appeals.description: Process for banned/timed-out members to appeal moderation actions.
flow: Banned member submits appeal via platform (not community-specific — platform-level form)
Appeal routed to community owner/admin queue
Owner/admin reviews with context (message history, mod action log)
Decision: uphold, overturn, or reduce penalty

trust_safety.description: Platform-level trust and safety beyond per-community moderation.
mechanisms: Content policy enforcement across all communities
User reporting system (report message, report user, report community)
Mod action audit log (who did what, when, to whom)

mod_action_log_table.description: Audit trail for all moderation actions within a community.

columns.name: action
columns.note: delete_message | pin | timeout | kick | ban | unban | role_change | lock_channel

columns.name: details
columns.note: Action-specific metadata (e.g., timeout_duration, old_role, new_role)

messaging.description: Direct messaging system: 1:1 DMs, group DMs, notifications, and read receipts. Separate from community channel messages.

dm_model.description: 1:1 direct messages between any two platform users. Already implemented via conversations + direct_messages tables.

gaps: No last_message_at for conversation list sorting
No last_message_preview for conversation list display

columns.name: reply_to_message_id
constraints: self-referential FK (defined in relations, not column)

gaps: read is per-message boolean, not per-participant — problematic for group DMs (is it read by whom?)
is_edited is nullable boolean (should be NOT NULL with default false)
reactions is json not jsonb (no indexing or partial update)
No content nullable for media-only messages
No last_read_message_id — cannot track unread count per participant
No left_at (no way to leave a group conversation without deleting the participant row)

group_dm.description: Group DMs for up to N users outside of community context. Already partially supported by conversations.is_group flag.
group_dm.current_note: conversations.is_group boolean and name/icon fields exist. conversation_participants supports multiple users. But read tracking is per-message not per-participant, and there is no max participant limit enforced.
desired_additions: Max participants limit (recommended: 10 for group DMs, unlimited for community channels)
Leave conversation (soft delete via left_at timestamp, not hard delete)

notifications.description: Notification system for community and messaging events.
notifications.current_note: notifications table exists with UUID PK. Supports generic type/message/read/linkTo fields. NotificationBell and NotificationPanel components exist. But no notification preferences, no push notifications, no notification batching.

notification_types_community.description: Someone @mentioned you in a channel message
Someone replied to your message in a channel
A new member joined your community (owner/admin only)
Your role was changed in a community
New announcement in a community you belong to

notification_types_messaging.description: You were added to a group conversation

delivery_channels.note: SendGrid dependency exists but no notification email templates
No service worker, no push subscription management

read_receipts.description: Read receipt model for DMs and community channels.

dm_read_model.current: direct_messages.read boolean per message — indicates sender knows recipient read it. Problematic for group DMs.
dm_read_model.desired: Per-participant read cursor via conversation_participants.last_read_message_id. Unread count = messages with id > last_read_message_id. For 1:1 DMs, read receipt shows when recipient's cursor passes the message.

channel_read_model.current: NOT_IMPLEMENTED — no read tracking for channel messages at all.
channel_read_model.desired: Per-user-per-channel read cursor stored in a channel_read_state table. Enables unread badge per channel and per community (sum of unread channels).

columns.name: last_read_message_id
columns.note: Null = never read. Points to the last message the user has seen.

columns.name: mention_count
columns.note: Unread @mentions since last_read_message_id

real_time.description: WebSocket infrastructure for community and messaging real-time features.

current.note: ws is installed. Unknown how much WebSocket logic exists in server code beyond dependency.

desired.auth: JWT or session token sent on connection upgrade. Connection rejected if invalid.
desired.reconnect_strategy: Exponential backoff starting at 1s, max 30s, with jitter
desired.subscription_model: Client subscribes to channels/conversations after auth. Server tracks active subscriptions per connection.
desired.scaling_note: Single-server WebSocket works for MVP. For scale: Redis pub/sub for multi-server fan-out, or hosted service (Ably, Pusher, Soketi).

events.description: Full event catalog for real-time system. Used by both community channels and DM conversations.

presence.description: User online/offline presence tracking within communities.

idle_detection.note: Client reports idle after 5 min inactivity. Server marks offline after 10 min without heartbeat.

typing_indicators.description: Visual indicator that another user is composing a message.

roles_permissions.description: Role-based access control for communities. Two layers: community-level roles and channel-level permission overrides.

current_status.description: Users have a global role field (text, default 'creator'). No community-level roles. No channel-level permissions.
current_status.note: The user.role field serves a different purpose (creator vs consumer platform role). It has nothing to do with community roles.

community_roles_table.description: Named roles within a community with ordered hierarchy and permission bundles.

columns.name: name
columns.note: e.g., 'Moderator', 'VIP', 'Team Lead'

columns.name: color
columns.note: Hex color for role name display in chat

columns.name: position
columns.note: Hierarchy order. Higher position = more authority. Owner is always highest.

columns.name: is_default
columns.note: Auto-assigned to new members. Only one default role per community.

columns.name: permissions
columns.note: Permission bundle: {send_messages: true, manage_messages: false, ...}

columns.name: is_mentionable
columns.note: Whether members can @mention this role

columns.name: is_hoisted
columns.note: Whether role members are displayed separately in the member list

builtin_roles.name: Owner
builtin_roles.note: Auto-created on community creation. Cannot be deleted or demoted. Full permissions.

channel_permission_overrides_table.description: Per-channel permission overrides for specific roles. Overrides the community-level role permissions for a specific channel.

columns.name: allow
columns.note: Permissions explicitly granted for this role in this channel

columns.name: deny
columns.note: Permissions explicitly denied for this role in this channel

channel_permission_overrides_table.permission_resolution: effective_permission(user, channel, perm) = (role.permissions[perm] OR channel_override.allow[perm]) AND NOT channel_override.deny[perm]. Deny always wins over allow. Higher-position roles checked first.

permission_keys.description: Complete list of permission keys used in role and channel override JSONB objects.

keys.description: Can send text messages in channels
Can add emoji reactions to messages
Can see messages sent before joining
Can delete or edit other users' messages
Can create, edit, delete roles (below own level)
Can edit member roles and nicknames
Can edit community settings, name, description, icon

current_code_truth.description: Summary of what exists in code today for community and messaging.

tables_exist.note: Name, description, icon_color, created_at. No owner, no membership.
Community FK, name, created_at. No type, no topic, no ordering.
Channel FK, user FK, content, is_pinned, likes, created_at. No reactions, no threading, no media.
DM containers with is_group flag, name, icon. Supports both 1:1 and group.
Junction with is_admin flag. Unique per user-conversation pair.
Most complete message table: content, read, is_edited, reply_to, reactions JSON. But no media, no types.

current_code_truth.implementation_detail: Tables defined in shared/schema.ts. Basic CRUD routes exist in server/routes.ts (the 53KB god file). Components: ChannelSidebar.tsx, ChatMessage.tsx, communities.tsx page. WebSocket dependency (ws 8.18.0) installed. Real-time implementation level unknown without route audit.
ui_components: pages/communities.tsx — community listing and channel view page

inconsistencies_between_tables.detail: channel_messages uses integer 'likes' count. direct_messages uses JSON 'reactions' object {userId: emoji}. Two different paradigms for the same concept in the same app.
inconsistencies_between_tables.recommendation: Standardize on reactions JSONB for both. Deprecate integer likes.

inconsistencies_between_tables.detail: direct_messages has reply_to_message_id for message threading. channel_messages has no threading at all.
inconsistencies_between_tables.recommendation: Add reply_to_id and thread_id to channel_messages to match DM pattern.

inconsistencies_between_tables.detail: direct_messages has is_edited (nullable boolean). channel_messages has no edit tracking.
inconsistencies_between_tables.recommendation: Add is_edited (NOT NULL default false) and edited_at to channel_messages.

inconsistencies_between_tables.detail: All community/messaging tables use serial integer PKs except notifications which uses UUID. New tables should standardize on UUID.
inconsistencies_between_tables.recommendation: New tables use UUID. Migration path: leave existing serial PKs but add UUID column for new references.

desired_vs_current_gap.description: Communities have no owner. No user can manage, configure, or monetize a community because there is no ownership relationship.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: communities table has no owner_user_id FK
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: owner_user_id FK to users table, plus optional business_id FK to businesses table

desired_vs_current_gap.description: No membership model. There is no way to track which users belong to which communities, at what tier, or with what permissions.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: community_members table with user, community, tier, role, ban/mute state, and notification preferences

desired_vs_current_gap.description: No paid tier model. Communities cannot be monetized because there is no way to define pricing tiers or connect to payment processing.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: No community_tiers table. No Stripe integration.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: community_tiers table with pricing fields and Stripe product/price IDs

desired_vs_current_gap.description: Channels have no type discriminator. All channels are implicitly text-only with no path to voice, video, announcement, forum, or stage channels.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: channels table has: id, community_id, name, created_at
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: type field (text|voice|video|announcement|forum|stage), topic, position, is_private, minimum_tier, slowmode_seconds

desired_vs_current_gap.description: No channel categories for organizing channels in the sidebar.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: No channel_categories table. Channels are a flat list per community.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: channel_categories table with name, position, community_id. Channels reference category_id.

desired_vs_current_gap.description: Channel messages lack reactions, threading, media attachments, edit tracking, and message types. Direct messages have some of these (reactions, reply_to, is_edited) but channel messages do not.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: channel_messages has: content, is_pinned, likes (integer). No reactions JSON, no reply_to, no is_edited, no attachments.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: Parity with DM model plus channel-specific features. reactions JSONB, reply_to_id, thread_id, attachments JSONB, message_type, is_edited, edited_at, deleted_at.

desired_vs_current_gap.description: No community role system. No RBAC for communities. The global user.role field (creator/consumer) is unrelated to community roles.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: No community_roles table. No channel_permission_overrides table.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: community_roles with hierarchy, permissions JSONB, color, mentionability. channel_permission_overrides for per-channel role overrides.

desired_vs_current_gap.description: No moderation system whatsoever. No auto-mod, no manual mod tools, no audit log, no ban management, no appeals.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: No moderation code or tables exist.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: Auto-mod rules (spam, word filter, link filter, rate limit), manual mod actions (delete, timeout, kick, ban), mod_action_log table, appeals flow.

desired_vs_current_gap.description: No read tracking for channel messages. DM read tracking uses a per-message boolean which does not scale to group contexts.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: No channel_read_state table. DMs use direct_messages.read boolean.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: channel_read_state table (per-user-per-channel cursor). DM read tracking via conversation_participants.last_read_message_id.

desired_vs_current_gap.description: No presence system. No typing indicators. Real-time message delivery may partially work via ws but is unverified.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: ws 8.18.0 is installed. No presence or typing indicator code identified from schema analysis.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: Full presence model (online/idle/dnd/offline/invisible), typing indicators with debounce, WebSocket subscription management.

desired_vs_current_gap.description: No voice or video channels. Requires WebRTC or third-party infrastructure.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: Voice channels (drop-in), video channels (camera + screen share), stage channels (broadcast with raise-hand).
desired_vs_current_gap.infrastructure_note: Requires WebRTC stack or third-party (LiveKit, Agora, 100ms, Twilio). Significant infrastructure investment. Recommended for post-MVP.

desired_vs_current_gap.description: DMs lack media attachments, message types, soft delete, and proper group DM read tracking.
desired_vs_current_gap.current: direct_messages has text content, reactions JSON, reply_to, is_edited. No media, no types, no soft delete.
desired_vs_current_gap.desired: message_type, attachments JSONB, deleted_at, content made nullable. conversation_participants gets last_read_message_id, is_muted, notification_preference, left_at.

open_questions.question: Voice and video infrastructure: build on WebRTC or buy third-party service (LiveKit, Agora, 100ms)?
open_questions.context: Voice/video channels require real-time media infrastructure that is complex to self-host. Third-party services charge per-minute. WebRTC is free but requires TURN/STUN servers and SFU for multi-user calls.

options.cons: High complexity, requires media server ops

options.pros: Open-source core, good SDK, can self-host or use cloud
options.cons: Cloud pricing at scale, self-hosting still requires ops

options.pros: Fastest to integrate, zero infrastructure ops
options.cons: Per-minute pricing, vendor lock-in, cost at scale

options.pros: Focus on text community first, validate demand
options.cons: Missing feature vs Discord, some creators need it

open_questions.recommendation: Option D for MVP, option B for post-MVP. Text communities are the core value. Voice/video is a nice-to-have that requires significant infra investment.

open_questions.question: Should community moderation use AI content analysis or rule-based only for MVP?
open_questions.context: Auto-mod can be rule-based (word lists, regex, rate limits) or AI-powered (sentiment analysis, toxicity scoring, context-aware). Rule-based is simpler and deterministic. AI is more nuanced but adds LLM cost and latency.

options.cons: Easily bypassed by creative spelling, no context awareness

options.pros: Better accuracy, handles edge cases, uses existing UMH intelligence routing
options.cons: Latency per message, LLM cost per message, potential false positives

options.description: Third-party moderation API (Perspective API, OpenAI moderation endpoint)
options.pros: Purpose-built, good accuracy, free or cheap tier
options.cons: External dependency, latency, data privacy concerns

open_questions.recommendation: Option A for MVP with clear path to B. UMH deterministic-first principle aligns: rule-based spine with AI enhancement when available.

open_questions.question: Should CreatorOS offer pre-built community templates (e.g., 'Coaching Community', 'Course Community', 'Fan Club')?
open_questions.context: Templates would pre-configure channel categories, channels, roles, and welcome messages for common creator use cases. Reduces setup friction for new creators. Discord has server templates as a feature.

options.description: No templates — blank slate with guided setup wizard
options.pros: Simpler to build, creators customize from scratch
options.cons: Higher friction, especially for creators who do not know Discord well

options.pros: Faster onboarding, best-practice defaults, differentiation from Discord
options.cons: Need to maintain templates, might not match all use cases
Complex to build, needs critical mass, post-MVP feature

open_questions.recommendation: Option B for MVP. 3-5 templates covering the most common creator community types: Coaching/Mastermind, Course Community, Fan Club, Product Support, General Creator.

open_questions.question: Should the serial-to-UUID PK migration happen during the community/messaging rebuild, or be deferred?
open_questions.context: Current tables use serial integer PKs. New tables are designed with UUID PKs. A mixed PK environment creates FK complexity. But migrating existing tables is a schema migration risk.

options.description: Add UUID columns to existing tables, FK new tables to UUID columns, leave serial as PK
Full migration to UUID PKs for all community/messaging tables
options.cons: Breaking migration, data must be re-keyed, all FKs updated

options.description: Keep serial PKs for existing tables, UUID for new tables only
options.cons: Permanent inconsistency, FKs between old and new tables awkward

open_questions.recommendation: Option C for now. New tables use UUID. Existing tables keep serial. Cross-references use the existing integer FK types. Revisit full migration when a breaking schema change is already planned.
